userFeedback: 四职业仍太清脆，需要更沉重；弓箭手不需要很长的风声，保留雷霆滋滋及各自材质。
production: Original deterministic material synthesis using installed NumPy/SciPy/FFmpeg; no recordings, AI model calls, downloads or new dependencies.
runtimeIntegration: Offline audition only; game runtime and all older studies preserved.
listeningAcceptance: Pending audition of heavier bodies and shorter bow air; frequency/energy metrics do not prove perceived weight or preference.

physical.userPreference: 2026-11-16: all professions should feel heavier and less bright; bow specifically must not have a long wind sound.
physical.provenance: Original deterministic NumPy/SciPy modelling with reused v5 material helpers; no recordings, AI, downloads, external samples or claimed listening approval.

sourceChanges.weight: Rebuilt finite 165-720Hz noise-excited compression and 180-700Hz wood/body layers become the main contact, rather than raising gain or lowering pitch on the old bright transient.
sourceChanges.war: The cutting edge has less energy and less high-frequency bandwidth; lower non-harmonic steel modes are damped behind the contact. No sine kick, hammer boom or chirp.
sourceChanges.bow: A firm string latch, low bow-limb resonance and weighted puncture replace bright snap-first balance. Shaft recoil stays separate from air.
sourceChanges.bowAir: V5 added 210ms wakes beginning 72-77ms after contact. Those wakes and the old longer release-air source are removed. New isolated packets last 50/60/65ms and are finished by 64/74/83ms, not merely hidden with EQ.

physical.tail: Darker finite material tails remain below contact; bows have no additional late air layer.
physical.mix: Active-window RMS balances individual material layers. Final .64 cap is protection only, not a uniform peak/loudness target.
physical.arrangement: Keep the v5 schedule/gain and cut preparation at actual release; these are source-timbre changes.
physical.acceptance: Frequency/envelope measures describe the changes; human and target-device listening acceptance remain pending.

elemental.userPreference: Less crisp and bright; more weight across professions while retaining accepted burst and longer material release.
elemental.provenance: Original deterministic procedural models using existing NumPy/SciPy and previous project source code. No downloads, recorded samples or AI calls.

sourceChanges.core: Accepted source is separated into low-mid pressure, middle texture and high edge. Bright edge is strongly reduced while the low-mid component is retained.
sourceChanges.newWeight: New finite noise excitation drives a non-harmonic bank around 149/211/303/437/591Hz with individually short damping; an independent turbulent pressure packet adds dense mass.
sourceChanges.fire: Additional low-mid rolling packets and reduced spark/ember edge produce thicker combustion. Finite breaths remain distinct from a constant noise wall.
sourceChanges.thunder: A newly authored short shock body supports the main contact and subordinate network groups; no descending sine kick, sub-bass dependency or long rumble.
sourceChanges.release: v5 fire/electric release is handled separately from impact weight. Electrical sizzle remains dense and sustained, with less high-frequency edge and a darker middle band.

elemental.spectralIntent: Weight is concentrated in the phone-audible 140–600Hz range; energy below 60Hz is rejected. This is a source-layer rebalance and added pressure model, not just one low-pass across the final sound.
elemental.mix: Peak cap .64, with no cue-by-cue loudness normalization. Audition comparison should match playback loudness.
elemental.acceptance: Frequency and envelope measurements verify source changes; perceived heaviness and naturalness require user listening.

designNotes.performance: V5 event gains and onsets are preserved; preparation ends at release, darker material bodies replace sharp layers, and bow air is kept short.

comparison.reference: PCM WAV; MP3 is a convenience preview and can shift gated loudness.
comparison.processing: Scalar gain only, no dynamics processor for matching.
